# EDI: Experimental Design and Inference

> EDI (Experimental Design and Inference) is an R package that marries
> randomized experimental designs — fixed (block, stratified, matched-pair,
> cluster, factorial, rerandomization, and MILP-based optimal designs) and
> sequential (matching-on-the-fly and covariate-adaptive designs: Atkinson,
> Efron, Pocock-Simon, urn) — with inference procedures (exact, asymptotic,
> distribution-free, and resampling-based) matched to each design and
> response type: continuous, incidence (binary), count, proportion, survival
> with censoring, and ordinal. Core estimation kernels are C++ (Eigen +
> LBFGS++). Not related to Electronic Data Interchange.

Key facts:

- Typical workflow: construct an R6 design object (e.g. `DesignSeqOneByOneKK21`,
  `DesignFixedBlocking`), assign treatments (all at once for fixed designs,
  one subject at a time for sequential designs), record responses, then run a
  matched inference class (e.g. `InferenceContinKKOLSIVWC`) or `InferenceSuite`,
  which runs every applicable procedure and reports one Cauchy-combined p-value.
- A built-in `SimulationFramework` supports power analysis and
  operating-characteristic studies across designs, response types, and
  inference procedures, with optional parallelization via `mirai`.
- The distinct Python package `edi_kernels` (PyPI) exposes the same C++
  model-fitting kernels with no R dependency.

## Installation (not on CRAN yet)

`install.packages("EDI")` fails today — the package exists but is awaiting
CRAN acceptance. Install prebuilt binaries from R-universe (Linux, macOS,
Windows; no compiler needed):

    install.packages("EDI", repos = c("https://kapelner.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

Fallback from GitHub (needs a C++ toolchain; the R package is the `R/EDI`
subdirectory, so `subdir` is required):

    remotes::install_github("kapelner/EDI", subdir = "R/EDI")

Python bindings: `pip install edi_kernels` (on PyPI).

## Machine-readable capability matrix (read this first)

"Which inference class supports which design family x response type x
method?" is answered by one generated file, exported straight from the
package's class registries (never hand-maintained; drift-checked on every
push):

- JSON, everything in one object:
  https://github.com/kapelner/EDI/blob/main/R/package_tests/capability_matrix.json
- CSV, one row per inference class (response_types, design_families,
  estimand, likelihood_tier, capabilities, public_methods, requires_*):
  https://github.com/kapelner/EDI/blob/main/R/package_tests/capability_matrix.csv
- CSV, one row per design class (timing_family, randomization_family,
  seed_reproducible_draw):
  https://github.com/kapelner/EDI/blob/main/R/package_tests/design_matrix.csv

`design_families` is the static compatibility declaration;
`design_level_exclusions` in the JSON is the per-instance rule applied on
top (currently: sequential DesignSeqOneByOne designs lose
nonparametric_bootstrap, except DesignSeqOneByOneBernoulli).
